findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text. Anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute permission, or any process able to reach the instance metadata user-data endpoint, can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No metadata_options block is configured, so the instance permits IMDSv1 token-less metadata requests. A server-side request forgery in the web application on this instance becomes credential theft against the instance role.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device configuration enables encryption, so the instance's root EBS volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

The instance is placed in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed to an internet gateway, giving it a public address directly reachable from the internet alongside a wide-open security group.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted and is not protected by a KMS key.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption or KMS key is specified, so a copy of the volume's data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored without key-based access control.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the host.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data-exfiltration path and a channel to command-and-control infrastructure if the host is compromised.
Port 80 is opened to 0.0.0.0/0 with no corresponding TLS listener, so all traffic between users and the web host travels in cleartext and is subject to interception or tampering.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the private network layer and exposing workloads that do not need inbound internet access.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the private network layer and exposing workloads that do not need inbound internet access.
The bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network audit data is written without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL restriction is defined for the flow log bucket, so a subsequent public ACL or bucket policy would not be blocked and network audit logs could be exposed.
The flow log bucket has force_destroy = true and no versioning, MFA delete, or object-lock protection, so the audit trail can be deleted or overwritten without trace.
